correctness.rationale: The all-ones trace forces every nonisolated support vertex to be either a source or a sink. In this bipartite support a three-edge simple path cannot have trace (1,0,1) on its consecutive edges, because its two outer edges fix the middle edge's labels to give 1. A connected bipartite graph with no such path is a star: if a vertex has two neighbors, any second incident edge at either neighbor produces a three-edge path, so every neighbor is a leaf, and connectedness exhausts the component. Conversely the fixed center label and independent leaf labels realize every star trace. Listing B increasingly and then its complement increasingly gives a one-descent word at most, and splitting at the descent represents every eligible word. For i<j, the inversion on the value pair is exactly i outside B and j in B. Thus centers must be extremal on their own component. All nonidentity words have unique B, and exactly n+1 choices of B give the identity. The n−1-edge minimum-label star gives the lower bound, and 2^n−n distinct concepts cannot realize the 2^n distinct leaves of a depth-n tree. At n=1 both dimensions are zero. For the EGF, labeled components of size r have edge weight z^(r−1) and multiplicity 1 for r=1,2 or 2 for r≥3. This also proves the maximum-support counts, with n=2 having one edge and n=1 the empty support.
residual_risks: The recorded exhaustion is only through n=6 for rankings and four vertices for general graphs. The result is not a sorting or identification-query complexity theorem.

value.rationale: The complete support classification resolves which sets of comparisons can vary independently, not just how many. It yields the edge-count distribution for all orders and describes its maximizers, while distinguishing the natural value-label problem from positional Grassmannian comparisons. The equality of static and adaptive dimensions is meaningful for this restricted ranking model, although the entropy bound itself is routine.
residual_risks: No identification algorithm, exact query complexity or general bounded-descent extension is asserted.
